operator_io_quirks: All table/column names are mixed-case CamelCase/snake_case; generated SQL must double-quote them ("Accounts", "account_id").
DDL uses backtick quoting; sqlite_master stores it verbatim; clone must replay CREATE TABLE text as-is.
Financial_Transactions has NO primary key (pk=[]); sample_fresh_primary_keys must be a no-op there, and drop_unique_duplicates has no unique columns to enforce.
transaction_id is NOT NULL but not PK; previous_transaction_id is a self-referencing-looking int with no declared FK (values 457..947, not in 1..15) — no FK edge, so no parent draw.
Two FKs on Financial_Transactions (account_id->Accounts.account_id, card_id->Customers_Cards.card_id) both point to existing single-column PKs; no dangling/non-unique parents here.
DATETIME columns store TEXT 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' (space separator, seconds, no T, no timezone); first element is not int-parseable so TS dispatches to Date, not Number.
date_valid_from/date_valid_to/transaction_date are declared DATETIME but storage class is text — declared type contradicts storage; affinity is NUMERIC-ish but values are strings.
transaction_amount is DOUBLE with storage 'real' (floats like 1701.23); Number fuzzer with scale from 'double' (no args) — check scale default.

Three columns are 100% NULL in the original (other_customer_details, transaction_comment, other_transaction_details); distinct=0, samples empty — literal pool contributes nothing, original_values are all None.
card_number and other_card_details hold long digit strings (13-16 chars) that look like card numbers; String fuzzer will treat them as int-like and add +-1 variants.

customer_phone has formats '(673)872-5338', '679-845-8645x94312', '1-511-656-6664' — mixed punctuation, extension suffix; String fuzzer's CHARSET lacks '-', '(', ')', 'x' so fresh values won't match format.
customer_address contains embedded newlines ('\n') and commas; String fuzzer CHARSET has no newline/comma, so fresh addresses lose structure.
Tables are tiny (15 rows each); read_schema sampling is trivial, no huge-table path exercised.
account_name holds zero-padded numeric strings ('038', '162'); String fuzzer int-like branch will produce '039'/'037' etc.
operator_ts_expectations: Date fuzzer on DATETIME columns: template inferred from first parsable element = '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S' (space, seconds); fresh dates formatted with that template.

Date range = [min,max] of parsed elements per column; date_valid_from spans 2009-2015, date_valid_to ~2018-03, transaction_date ~2018-03 — narrow ranges, so fresh dates cluster tightly (likely FN on range predicates outside these windows).

Number fuzzer on INTEGER PKs (account_id, customer_id, card_id, transaction_id): scale from 'integer' (no args) -> default scale; fresh ints perturbed by +-1/+-2, so PKs stay near 1..15 and collide often -> sample_fresh_primary_keys drops many rows.

Number fuzzer on transaction_amount (DOUBLE): scale from 'double' default; range [-10^s,10^s]; fresh floats perturbed by +-0.01/+-0.02 — plausible amounts, but original amounts are 100s-1000s so fresh draws may be too small (FN on amount thresholds).

String fuzzer on card_type_code / transaction_type (2 distinct values 'Credit'/'Debit', 'Payment'/'Refund'): p=0.2 fresh random strings over a-zA-Z0-9() will inject garbage values -> FP on equality/IN filters, FN on 'Credit'/'Debit' grouping.
String fuzzer on customer_first_name/last_name: fresh random strings, not name-like; original names are Faker-style — TS will produce implausible names (FN on LIKE 'A%' style predicates).
String fuzzer on customer_email: fresh random strings lack '@' and '.', so email-format predicates (LIKE '%@%') will match nothing -> FN.
String fuzzer on customer_phone: fresh strings lack '-', '(', ')', 'x' -> phone-format predicates FN.
String fuzzer on card_number: int-like branch adds +-1 variants; fresh random strings over CHARSET produce non-numeric garbage -> card-number length/format predicates FN.

FK columns account_id/card_id in Financial_Transactions draw from parent's FINAL filtered values with replacement -> duplicates common; original has 13/10 distinct out of 15, so ties are plausible (not a miss).

100%-NULL columns: original_values all None -> Base drops None -> no elements -> p:=1 -> always fresh random strings; original has only NULLs, so any IS NULL predicate will FP (fresh non-null values).

No PK on Financial_Transactions: no PK dedup, no unique dedup -> duplicate transaction_id rows possible; original has distinct=15 so duplicates are a new behaviour (FP on COUNT(DISTINCT transaction_id)).

previous_transaction_id has no FK and values 457..947 (not in 1..15): Number fuzzer will draw near 1..15 (perturbation of sampled elements) -> loses the 'points to another transaction' semantics (FN on self-join predicates).
